records.statement: The unsigned article “Lucubratio Ebria” (The Press, Christchurch, 29 July 1865) rejects a previous correspondent's view that machines are separate beings whose final triumph over mankind is to be expected, and treats machines as the means by which the human organism develops.

time.note: The Press, vol. VIII, issue 847, p. 2, in the Papers Past record.

engagement.rationale: Gives a reason against the premise that machines are a separate kind of being that could succeed people: they are extensions of the human organism.

records.qualification: The article frames itself as a dream after a glass of hot whisky and water and closes by leaving 'our dream'. Its attribution to Butler rests on its close match with the reply to the machine treatise in Erewhon (1872), as the dataset's entity records. The same passage is the evidence of the dataset's B6 record of this article (ts-b6-butler-1865-contests). The quotation is read in the Papers Past OCR text; the newspaper page image was not checked (Papers Past image requests answered HTTP 403 to the cross-family check and on 2026-11-03 here).

evidence.note: The omitted words are 'to animalise them,' (OCR 'aniinalise').

records.statement: Erewhon (1872) gives, as an extract from a fictional Erewhonian treatise, the question whether people are not themselves creating their successors in the supremacy of the earth, giving machines ever more of a self-regulating, self-acting power that will be better than intellect.

time.note: Title-page year of the 1872 Trübner printing.

records.qualification: Fiction: the narrator of a satirical novel translates extracts from a treatise that led Erewhon to destroy its machines; the passage documents what the novel says, not Butler's view. The passage is put as a rhetorical question. Butler's letter of 1863, already recorded on W01, has a close counterpart sentence.

evidence.passage: Are we not ourselves creating our successors in the supremacy of the earth? daily adding to the beauty and delicacy of their organisation, daily giving them greater skill and supplying more and more of that self-regulating self-acting power which will be better than intellect itself?
